# SPD-092 — A suite run went red once while Spud wrote the real ledger during it, and nothing in the suite names the cause

## Brief
While landing SPD-086 the full suite was run three times on the same code: twice green on the ticket's branch (876 OK, Cascade's run and Spud's) and once on merged `main`, where it reported `Ran 876 tests ... FAILED (failures=1)`. The failing test's name and traceback were lost -- the run was piped through `tail -6`, which kept only the summary -- and an immediate rerun of the identical tree was `876 OK`. So this is one observed red with no name attached to it, recorded rather than explained away.

What was different about the failing run, and the hypothesis worth testing first: Spud was writing the **real** ledger database concurrently (`member finish`, `ticket edit`) and editing the real `CLAUDE.md` while it ran. Tests build their own homes under a temp directory, so no test should notice either; if one does, that is the finding, and it is adjacent to [[SPD-083]], where two suite runs in one checkout read each other's in-flight source.

The other difference is that merged `main` carried another session's rendered `ledger/` and `reports/` markdown that the branch did not. No test should read those either.

Reproduce deliberately: run the suite while a loop writes the real ledger through the CLI (`ticket edit --outcome`, `member log`) and rewrites `CLAUDE.md`, and see whether a test fails. If one does, the fix is to make it independent of the real home; if nothing fails after a fair number of attempts, say so and close this -- an unreproducible red is worth one honest attempt, not an open-ended hunt.

Worth doing whatever the outcome: the suite is run before every landing, so a run whose failure detail can be discarded by a pipe is a hole in the landing evidence. Consider whether the documented command in CLAUDE.md's Commands section should capture full output to a file rather than be piped.

## Size, persona and model decision
One researcher, or one engineer if the reproduction is quick: the work is to reproduce deliberately, not to guess.
